title: [Icons-Only Task Manager] When not Grouped, Icons of Pinned Programs cannot be drag-placed past where Pinned Programs would be when Grouped
line: With grouping off, windows of pinned apps can now be dragged anywhere among the pinned apps, and other apps' windows can no longer be dropped among them.
explanation: In the Icons-only Task Manager (launch-in-place sorting), TasksModel::move() put the barrier between pinned and unpinned tasks at the number of launchers. Without grouping each launcher can be replaced by several window tasks, so the real pinned area is longer: pinned windows couldn't be dropped past the launcher-count slot, and unpinned windows could be dropped into the tail of the pinned area. The barrier is now the number of leading rows that are launchers or launcher-backed tasks.

commits.message:
libtaskmanager: let ungrouped pinned windows move in the whole pinned area

With launch-in-place sorting, the barrier between pinned and unpinned tasks
was the number of launchers, but without grouping one launcher can be shown
as several windows. The barrier now counts the launcher-backed rows instead.

BUG: 501112

media.caption: Launchers Konsole, Dolphin, System Settings; ungrouped, 3 Konsole and 2 Dolphin windows. Dragging the active Konsole onto System Settings stops at slot 3.
Same drag with the fix: the Konsole window follows the pointer past the Dolphin windows and stays next to System Settings.
After the drop: the Konsole window is stuck at slot 3.
After the drop: the Konsole window sits where it was dropped, still in the pinned area.
Dragging Info Center (not pinned) left: it enters the pinned area and stays between the Konsole and Dolphin windows.
Same drag with the fix: Info Center stays after the pinned area.
After the drop: Info Center is inside the pinned area.
After the drop: Info Center is still last.

review.text: Counting the leading launcher and launcher-backed rows in TasksModel::move() for launchInPlace mode fixes the exact root cause cleanly in libtaskmanager and matches the predicate already used by lessThan() and updateManualSortMap(). Both halves of the bug (pinned ungrouped windows unable to move across the full pinned block, and unpinned windows able to enter it) are thoroughly verified with before/after media and regression checks across grouped and ungrouped modes.
